scope: Library artwork appearance while scrolling, without changes to game injection, Steam credentials or game renderers.
cause: Disk images were resident after about 50 ms, but composing full card bitmaps on Main with a per-display-tick budget delayed the last visible cards beyond 500 ms.
behavior: Two bounded user-initiated workers compose immutable card snapshots. AppKit views, artwork bindings, catalog state and card-layer assignment remain on Main.
Prepared symbols are captured once on Main; workers own their bitmap and thread-local drawing context.
Visible cards take priority over up to four directional look-ahead rows and one trailing row, limited to the tile cache byte budget. Only visible/adjacent rows own card layers.
Viewport/key changes cancel stale work; completed cards publish in default, event-tracking and modal modes. The display link can sleep while workers are busy.
Gameplay/resource cleanup cancels tile requests and clears card layers, decoded artwork and composed tile images. Late completions cannot repopulate released graphics.

comparison.conditions: Matching actual library/cache copies, network disabled, hidden nonactivated UI, deliberately blocked background index writer, default and event-tracking modes. Cold viewport jump positions are unchanged. Final continuous-scroll test is faster (48 points per step versus baseline 8).
comparison.timestampMeaning: Time from entry into the modeled viewport to actual artwork in an immutable tile assigned to a visible card layer; not an on-glass timestamp.

limits: No measured on-screen input-to-pixel latency or continuous-scroll frame pacing claim. Live normal-library checks are functional observations.
Uncached artwork still requires network transfer; unavailable publisher artwork retains the existing fallback.
No new native-game FPS, overlay GPU-performance or game compatibility measurement.
